blocking_issues: New H3 'If you live overseas or only one of you is Australian': the age sentence applies s 88D(3) (under 16, neither domiciled in Australia) under a heading that equates nationality with domicile and omits s 88D(2)(b) for couples where one partner was domiciled here (edit 1).

New H3 passport line says citizens living overseas can sometimes use a legalised Italian certificate, omitting fact_21's citizen-before-marriage condition and fact_20's rule that Australian-born citizens always need an Australian name change certificate (edit 2).
New H3 claims the Wedded Advisor 'confirms anything particular to your situation' (personal legal advice); not in brand-facts.md and against the compliance wording rule (edit 3).
Queensland row's added sentence is a circular, unactionable rendering of fact_29 (edit 4).
'A fee applies' for NSW/Victorian change of name has no source in the pack (edit 5).

edits.location: H2 'The legal test', H3 'If you live overseas or only one of you is Australian', paragraph 1, sentence 2
edits.issue: BLOCKING (legal). Matches fact_06 (s 88D(3)) literally, but under a heading that equates nationality with domicile it tells a couple where one partner is Australian (and likely domiciled here) that the under-16 rule is theirs. When either party was domiciled in Australia, s 88D(2)(b) applies instead (marriageable age under Part II, fact_05). 'Simpler' also mischaracterises a lower threshold.
edits.fix: Replace "Where neither of you is domiciled in Australia, the age rule is simpler, and the marriage is not recognised while either of you is under 16. <!-- fact_06 -->" with "If either of you was domiciled in Australia at the wedding, both of you must have been of marriageable age under Australian law; if neither was, the marriage is not recognised while either of you is under 16. <!-- fact_05 --> <!-- fact_06 -->"

edits.issue: BLOCKING (legal). 'Citizens living overseas can sometimes use a legalised, translated Italian certificate' omits both conditions: fact_21 requires citizenship before the marriage, and fact_20 says an Australian-born citizen who marries overseas always needs an Australian name change certificate, wherever they live. Most readers in this H3 (Australian-born, living abroad) would wrongly think the Italian certificate works for them.
edits.fix: Replace "Citizens living overseas can sometimes use a legalised, translated Italian certificate for a passport (see the table below), and embassies keep lists of approved translators. <!-- fact_21 --> <!-- fact_22 -->" with "Living overseas does not change the passport rule for Australian-born citizens, who always need an Australian name change certificate; a legalised Italian certificate, translated in full by an accredited translator, is accepted only if you were born overseas and became a citizen before marrying. <!-- fact_20 --> <!-- fact_21 --> <!-- fact_22 -->"

edits.issue: BLOCKING (brand claim). 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms anything particular to your situation' after domicile and visa points implies the Advisor gives personal legal advice. brand-facts.md supports no such claim, and the compliance checklist allows only 'the Advisor confirms current requirements, rather than giving legal advice'. It also contradicts the closing 'not legal advice' line.
edits.fix: Replace "Your Wedded Advisor confirms anything particular to your situation." with "Your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements for your dates, and a family lawyer can advise on domicile or anything else particular to your situation."

edits.location: H2 'Changing your surname', H3 'Other states and territories', table, Queensland row
edits.issue: BLOCKING (legal clarity). The added second sentence ('If you had earlier changed your name with the Registry to your partner's, change it at the Registry') is circular and does not say what to change it to; it compresses fact_29's condition into an instruction a reader cannot act on and may misread. The first half is supported and is enough for the table.
edits.fix: Replace "| Queensland | Not always automatic; some organisations need an official change of name. If you had earlier changed your name with the Registry to your partner's, change it at the Registry <!-- fact_29 --> |" with "| Queensland | You may not be able to take your partner's name automatically, and some organisations need an official change of name document <!-- fact_29 --> |"

edits.location: H3 'NSW and Victoria: a change of name application', last sentence
edits.issue: BLOCKING (fee claim). 'A fee applies' is a new, unmarked factual claim; neither fact_27 (NSW) nor fact_28 (Victoria) mentions a fee, and the source pack holds no registry fee. No figure is stated, so nothing goes to Nic, but the assertion itself is unsupported.
edits.fix: Replace "A fee applies; check your registry's page for the current fee and timing." with "Check your registry's page for any fee and the current processing time."
